title: Pow! (Forward)
label: Relentless Records
format: Digital (iTunes) first, then physical CD and vinyl. The OCC lists RELDX15. Wikipedia mentions a vinyl version with a longer Hotshot verse.

type.basis: An eight-bar rally over Dexplicit's Forward Riddim; its producer singles out the 808 kick as new to grime.

sound.text: An 'eight-bar rally': each MC delivers a short verse with no chorus or breaks, over two alternating eight-bar loops.

RA describes an 8-bar instrumental with a stark, bouncy synthline, claps and a militaristic fanfare. Its producer, D'Explicit, quoted by RA, says the bass enters with no intro and singles out the 808 kick as new to grime.

Wikipedia says Dexplicit was reportedly among the first grime producers to use American hip-hop samples and 808 drums in place of UK garage influences, and built the beat in FL Studio in under an hour.
Simon Reynolds (Spin, 2005) called it 'a massive jolt of sonic adrenaline' built on a 'frantic' riddim.

context.text: Peaked at no. 11 on the Official Singles Chart (first chart date 01/01/2005, 7 weeks) and at no. 1 on the Official Dance Singles Chart.
Won the MOBO Award for Best Single in 2005. Some London and South East venues and radio stations banned it, and Bizzle answered with 'Do not play Lethal Bizzle' T-shirts.
The featured MCs come mostly from East London crews including More Fire Crew, East Connection, N.A.S.T.Y. Crew and Roll Deep.
Reynolds (2005) called it grime's biggest UK hit to that date and noted airplay from Funkmaster Flex on Hot 97 in the US.

rels.other: 'Forward Riddim' (Dexplicit). Chantelle Fiddy, Nov 2004: 'Pow' is a version of the Forward Riddim with a new name and a changed structure
'Da Bizzle Remix' (B-side, same riddim, Face replaces D Double E)
Lethal Bizzle - 'Pow 2011' (feat. JME, Wiley, Chip, P Money, Ghetts, Kano), a new version, not a remix

uncertainty: Release dates conflict: Wikipedia gives digital 25 Oct 2004 and physical 20 Dec 2004, RA says October 2004, and Fiddy (8 Nov 2004) expected an official release in November. Catalogue numbers: the OCC lists RELDX15 and RA lists RELT 15. Formats were not confirmed per catalogue number. Discogs lists separate 'Lethal B - Forward Riddim' releases, but Discogs could not be fetched, so the instrumental's own release details are unverified.
tracklist: Wikipedia says the B-side 'Da Bizzle Remix' features nearly all of the original artists, with Face replacing D Double E.
